keyConcerns.headline: Operating reserves are calculated from the FY2022 Form 990, not the FY2024 income statement above

strengths_deep_dive: Primary operational strengths stem from targeted direct service delivery in crisis zones. Despite structural accounting risks, MedGlobal deploys staff and supplies to active disaster regions, serving patients across <cite id="6">67 health facilities</cite> in active conflict zones. The organization also maintains a low fundraising cost structure, expending <cite id="12">$0.13 per $1 raised</cite>.
rich_narrative.summary: MedGlobal faces primary operational and evaluative limiting factors due to significant gifts-in-kind reliance and governance data gaps. In FY2024, the organization reported a <cite id="13">Total Revenue of $33,542,803</cite>, but 94% of this revenue consisted of non-cash contributions. When adjusting for gifts-in-kind, MedGlobal operates with a <cite id="12">cash-adjusted program expense ratio of 70.7%</cite>, which sits below the <cite id="12">peer program ratio median of 89.2%</cite> and the <cite id="12">industry standard benchmark of 75%</cite>. Additionally, the organization lacks a documented theory of change and maintains weak board governance visibility. On direct medical delivery, MedGlobal responds to health crises by supporting facilities in regions including <cite id="2">Syria, Yemen, and Gaza</cite>. The charity is <cite id="4">ZAKAT-ELIGIBLE</cite> and holds an <cite id="12">overall rating of 88.0/100 from Charity Navigator</cite>.
